jobs.title: Product Manager: Console
jobs.description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.




ROLE OVERVIEW



We're hiring a strong, hands-on Product Manager to own the application side of the CodeRabbit Management Console, the surfaces every customer touches to set up, configure, control access to, and pay for CodeRabbit. This is a high-ownership IC role with a clear path to build and lead a team once you've settled in and proven impact.

You'll own organization settings, review configuration, role-based access control, billing and subscriptions, and the onboarding experience. Getting these right is foundational to our move upmarket and to our growth.

This isn't an AI-glamour role. It's a complex, technically demanding, and deeply important one. We want someone who sees that clearly and is excited by it, not someone chasing the next shiny AI feature.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN




CONSOLE, SETTINGS & CONFIGURATION

 - Own the end-to-end product experience for organization-level settings, team management, and review configuration

 - Make complex configuration understandable and accessible for both technical admins and non-technical buyers, without dumbing it down

 - Work closely with engineering to define APIs, UI flows, and data models for configuration that scale across teams, repos, and deployment types


ACCESS CONTROL: RBAC & CUSTOM ROLES

 - Own the permission model end to end: define the roles, scopes, and capabilities that govern who can see and do what across settings, configuration, billing, and member management

 - Ship custom roles so admins can define their own permission sets rather than being boxed into our defaults, the table-stakes capability that unblocks larger, more security-conscious buyers

 - Get permission granularity and scoping right: org-level vs. team-level vs. repo-level access, and the inheritance and override behavior between them

 - Own audit logs and access trails, who changed what and when, as both an enterprise requirement and a pillar of our security and compliance posture

 - Treat least-privilege defaults, clear permission surfaces, and "no surprises" access behavior as core to the design, not afterthoughts


BILLING & SUBSCRIPTION MANAGEMENT

 - Own the billing product: pricing display, plan management, seat-based licensing, upgrades and downgrades, and invoicing

 - Reduce friction in the purchase and upgrade path; design self-serve flows with correct proration, and partner with Growth and Sales on conversion and expansion

 - Own plan entitlements and feature gating, the mapping between what someone pays for and what they can actually use, kept consistent across the whole app

 - Handle the subscription lifecycle edge cases that quietly break trust: seat reconciliation and true-ups, renewals, failed payments and dunning, downgrades, and mid-cycle changes

 - Support enterprise purchasing: annual contracts, PO-based and offline billing, tax and invoicing requirements

 - Partner with Finance and Engineering on lifecycle correctness, and own the relationship with our billing infrastructure (Stripe, Chargebee, or similar)


ONBOARDING & ACTIVATION

 - Own the onboarding wizard and first-run experience for new organizations and individual users

 - Drive activation metrics: time-to-first-review, time-to-team-invite, and setup completion rates

 - Identify and eliminate the top drop-off points in the setup funnel




WHO YOU ARE



 - 5+ years of product management experience, ideally at a B2B SaaS or developer tools company

 - Technically fluent. You can read code, understand APIs, and have detailed conversations with engineers without a translator

 - Track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder product areas such as admin consoles, permissions/RBAC systems, or billing systems, where correctness and edge cases matter as much as the happy path

 - Strong instincts for simplifying complex configuration and access experiences without dumbing them down

 - Comfortable with ambiguity; can move from fuzzy problem to clear spec without hand-holding

 - You write well and communicate precisely. PRDs and tickets you've written are things you're proud of

 - Low ego, high ownership. You care about the outcome more than the credit




NICE TO HAVE



 - Prior experience at a developer tooling, DevOps, or code intelligence company

 - Direct experience with RBAC, permissions, or identity/access systems, designing role models, scopes, and audit logging

 - Experience with billing infrastructure (Stripe, Chargebee, or similar) and subscription lifecycle mechanics

 - Familiarity with multi-tenant SaaS architectures, and with audit/compliance requirements (SOC 2 and similar)

 - Working knowledge of Git platforms (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, ADO) as a power user or PM

 - You've worked with or alongside a small, high-output engineering team and know how to match their pace




WHAT THIS ISN'T



We'll be upfront: this role isn't primarily about building AI features. If what excites you most is prompt engineering, model evaluation, or shipping AI-native UX, this probably isn't your best fit right now.

What it is: one of the most important, highest-leverage product bets we're making. The companies that win in developer tooling are the ones who nail the unglamorous stuff, setup, configuration, access control, billing, and trust. We need someone who genuinely believes that.




WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH



You'll partner closely with our engineering leads (frontend, backend, SRE), the head of design, and with Finance, Growth, and Sales on the billing and activation surfaces. You'll report into Product leadership and work alongside a tight-knit, high-output India engineering team that moves fast and expects the same from product.



OUR VALUES

 

 1. 🤝 Collaborative Humans: Prioritizing collective intelligence

 2. 🚀 Fearless Innovators: Turning obstacles into growth opportunities

 3. 💪 Persistent, Passionate Developers: Thriving on complex, long-term challenges

 4. 🎯 Impact-Driven Creators: Crafting intuitive tools for developers

 5. 🧠 Rapid Learners and Un-learners: Adapting quickly in our fast-paced technological world

 


WHAT WE OFFER

 

 1. Work on cutting-edge technology with real-world impact

 2. Collaborative and innovative environment

 3. Competitive salary, equity, and benefits

 4. Professional development opportunities

 

To apply, submit your resume and relevant project samples or GitHub profiles. CodeRabbit is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion.

jobs.title: Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.



The Role

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who lives in the funnel. At our volume a 5% delta in onboarding completion or trial-to-paid conversion is a material business result. You will own the experimentation roadmap across acquisition, activation, and conversion, and you will be measured on moving those numbers. This is not a people-management role: you will lead through influence, data, and shipped experiments, partnering with engineering, design, and growth marketing.

What You Will Do

 - Own the PLG funnel end to end: activation, onboarding completion, trial-to-paid conversion, and expansion across web, CLI, and VS Code.

 - Identify the highest-leverage drop-off points through funnel analysis, then design and ship experiments to fix them.

 - Build and run a continuous experimentation program: hypotheses, instrumentation, A/B tests, and clear readouts on what won, what lost, and why.

 - Optimize across surfaces with their distinct dynamics: frictionless web signup, CLI auth and first-run experience, and VS Code install-to-active-use.

 - Improve onboarding for non-primary providers (GitLab and others), where activation has historically lagged the GitHub path.

 - Partner with engineering to instrument events properly so every funnel step is measurable.

 - Define and own North Star and input metrics, and make the tradeoffs visible to leadership.

What You Bring

 - 5 to 8 years in product management, with a meaningful stretch owning growth or PLG funnels.

 - A track record of measurable funnel wins: conversion lift, activation improvement, retention gains, with the numbers to back it.

 - Strong quantitative instinct: comfortable in SQL, amplitude or mixpanel class tools, and reasoning about statistical significance.

 - Experimentation rigor: you design clean tests, respect sample size, and resist shipping on vibes.

 - A developer-product sensibility: you understand why CLI, IDE, and web users behave differently.

 - Strong written communication and the ability to drive cross-functional work without authority.

Nice to Have

 - Experience with developer tools, devtools PLG, or technical audiences.

 - Familiarity with bottoms-up SaaS motions and self-serve to sales-assist handoffs.

 - Exposure to AI or code-adjacent products.

jobs.description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.




ROLE OVERVIEW

We're hiring a strong, hands-on Product Manager to own CodeRabbit's security product: the AI-driven scanner that hunts for real vulnerabilities across entire codebases and surfaces security findings directly in pull request reviews. The product combines LLM-based vulnerability hunting with static analysis, secrets detection, infrastructure-as-code checks, and dependency and supply-chain analysis, and grades every finding for exploitability and severity before a customer ever sees it.

This is a high-ownership IC role.

One thing we're firm on: you must come from the security space. This product lives or dies on security judgment - what a true positive looks like, what severity a finding deserves, and what an AppSec team actually needs before it will trust a scanner.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN




PRODUCT DIRECTION & ROADMAP

 - Own the security product end to end: deep codebase scans, security findings in pull request reviews, and everything in between

 - Decide which vulnerability classes, scanner capabilities, and languages we invest in next across SAST, secrets detection, infrastructure-as-code misconfiguration, and dependency and supply-chain analysis

 - Define what good detection means as a product: the precision, recall, and noise bar a finding must clear before a customer sees it




THE FINDINGS EXPERIENCE

 - Own how findings are presented, triaged, and resolved: severity and exploitability grading, dismissal and feedback loops, remediation flows, and reporting

 - Treat every false positive as a trust problem, not a tuning detail — the goal is a scanner developers believe, not one they mute

 - Turn detection-quality evidence (benchmarks, evaluations, real-world results) into product decisions and customer-facing proof




THE SECURITY BUYER

 - Own the AppSec and CISO persona alongside our developer users: what security teams need to evaluate, trust, and roll out the product across an organization

 - Partner with Sales on enterprise security evaluations and competitive positioning in the code security market

 - Shape pricing and packaging of the security offering with Growth and Finance


DETECTION QUALITY AS A PRODUCT METRIC

 - Work daily with the engineers building the agentic scanning pipeline; bring the customer and market view to detection priorities

 - Own the quality bar for what ships: hold detection changes to benchmark evidence, and make precision-versus-coverage tradeoffs deliberately rather than by default




WHO YOU ARE

 - 5–8 years in the security space: product management at a security vendor, or hands-on security work (application security, penetration testing, vulnerability research, detection engineering) that you carried into product. We're hiring security depth, not adjacent experience

 - Product management experience with deeply technical products, ideally at a B2B SaaS or developer tools company

 - Practical knowledge of real vulnerability classes and how they're exploited — enough to challenge a severity call, judge a disputed false positive, and hold your own with security engineers and customers' AppSec teams

 - You know the security tooling landscape (SAST, DAST, secrets scanning, IaC, software composition analysis) and exactly why developers distrust most of it

 - Technically fluent. You can read code, understand APIs, and have detailed conversations with engineers without a translator

 - You write well and communicate precisely. PRDs and tickets you've written are things you're proud of

 - Comfortable with ambiguity; can move from fuzzy problem to clear spec without hand-holding

 - Low ego, high ownership. You care about the outcome more than the credit
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - A hands-on practitioner past: CVEs, bug bounty history, CTFs, or pentest findings with your name on them

 - Experience shipping products built on LLMs or agentic systems, or well-formed judgment about where they help and where they fail

 - Direct vendor-side experience in the code security market (SAST, ASPM, or software composition analysis)

 - Working knowledge of Git platforms (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, ADO) as a power user or PM




WHAT THIS ISN'T

We'll be upfront: this isn't a compliance-checkbox product, and it isn't a GTM-only role. The hard problems here are detection quality, trust, and making security findings genuinely actionable for developers - deep, technical, judgment-heavy product work in one of the fastest-moving areas of AI.

What it is: one of the biggest product bets we're making. As AI writes more of the world's code, someone has to catch what it gets wrong, and we intend to be the ones developers and security teams both trust to do it.




OUR VALUES

🤝 Collaborative Humans: Prioritizing collective intelligence

🚀 Fearless Innovators: Turning obstacles into growth opportunities

💪 Persistent, Passionate Developers: Thriving on complex, long-term challenges

🎯 Impact-Driven Creators: Crafting intuitive tools for developers

🧠 Rapid Learners and Un-learners: Adapting quickly in our fast-paced technological world




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Work on cutting-edge technology with real-world impact

 - Collaborative and innovative environment

 - Competitive salary, equity, and benefits

 - Professional development opportunities





To apply, submit your resume and relevant project samples or GitHub profiles. CodeRabbit is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion.

jobs.title: Product Manager - All Levels
jobs.description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Product at CodeRabbit sits at the intersection of developer empathy, frontier AI capabilities, and real commercial stakes. As a Product Manager, you will shape how millions of developers experience AI-powered code review across IDEs, Git platforms, the CLI, and the web — surfaces where the playbook hasn't been written yet and the models improve under your feet every quarter.

Our work decides whether CodeRabbit feels like noise or like a trusted teammate: whether a developer acts on a review comment, adopts an agentic workflow, or brings CodeRabbit to their whole organization. You will live close to both the customer and the model — talking to developers weekly, prototyping with AI tools yourself, and translating what's newly possible into products people rely on.

We are hiring across all levels, and we mean it. If you are early in your product career with sharp instincts and a bias for shipping, we will give you real ownership from week one. If you are a seasoned product leader or former founder who has taken products from zero to category-defining scale, we will give you problems worthy of that experience — and room to shape the product organization itself. We will calibrate scope, title, and compensation to you, not the other way around.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Depending on your experience, you will own a surface, a product line, or the roadmap itself. Across levels, the work looks like this:

 - Own problems end-to-end. Drive discovery, definition, and delivery — from customer conversations and data analysis through specs, launch, and iteration — for products developers use every day.

 - Stay close to the customer. Build relationships with the developers and engineering leaders who use CodeRabbit, run feedback loops with our largest customers, and turn what you hear into what we build.

 - Stay close to the model. Understand what frontier models can do today and where they're heading, and design products for the capabilities arriving next — not just the ones already here.

 - Prototype to learn. Use AI tools to build and validate ideas yourself before committing engineering resources. The cheapest way to answer a product question is often to build the answer.

 - Ship fast and measure honestly. Get work in front of users quickly, define what success looks like before launch, and let adoption and retention — not opinions — settle debates.

 - Partner deeply with engineering, design, and go-to-market. Work fluently with technical teams on how things get built, and with sales and marketing on how they land.

 - Bring structure to ambiguity. Much of this space has no precedent. You'll frame the problem, propose the path, and rally the team around it rather than waiting for direction.

 - For senior folks: raise the bar. Define product strategy across surfaces, mentor other PMs, and help build the product culture and team around you.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Sharp product judgment. You form clear points of view from customer conversations, usage data, and your own use of the product — and you change them when the evidence says to. This is the core of the role, at every level.

 - You ship. You would rather get something in front of users this week than perfect it for a month, and you take pride in what happens after launch, not just the launch itself.

 - You're AI-native in how you work. You already use AI tools daily to extend what you can do — prototyping, analyzing, writing — and you have informed opinions about where these tools fall short.

 - You're technical enough to be dangerous. You can go deep with engineers on how something works, read a pull request, and understand why a model behaves the way it does. An engineering background helps but isn't required.

 - You communicate to drive decisions. You write clearly, bring clarity out of complexity, and influence without authority — whether the audience is an engineer, a customer, or the executive team.

 - You're energized by ambiguity. Emerging AI product surfaces have few conventions. You see that as the opportunity, not the obstacle.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

We care far more about the shape of your experience than its length. You might be a great fit whether you have 2 years of experience or 20:

 - Experience building products for developers or other technical users — as a PM, founder, engineer who moved into product, or in an equivalent role.

 - A track record of shipping: products, features, or prototypes that real users adopted, at whatever scale your role afforded.

 - Evidence of ownership beyond your job description — the project you drove because it needed driving.

 - For senior candidates: experience taking products from 0-to-1 or 1-to-scale, owning outcomes (revenue, adoption, retention) and not just roadmaps, or building and leading product teams.

Nice to have

 - Experience at developer-focused companies (e.g., GitHub, Vercel, Postman, Datadog) or on AI/ML-powered products.

 - A background in or strong understanding of software development and Git workflows.

 - Founder or early-stage operator experience, where you owned commercial outcomes.

 - Experience with product-led growth, platform integrations, or enterprise adoption motions.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - The chance to define the product direction for a category-defining AI product used by millions of developers.

 - Real ownership at every level — juniors get surfaces to own, seniors get strategy to set.

 - A collaborative, high-velocity environment working alongside strong engineers and AI researchers.

 - Competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits — calibrated to your level and experience.

 - Professional development and the resources to do the best work of your career.

We encourage you to apply even if you don't match everything above. Strong product people come from unusual paths, and "all levels" means exactly that — if this problem space excites you, we want to hear from you.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.




SENIOR/STAFF PRODUCT MARKETING MANAGER

CodeRabbit helps engineering teams understand, verify, govern, and ship code; whether the change starts in a pull request, an IDE, a terminal, or an agent workflow. We're hiring a Senior/Staff Product Marketing Manager to own the market story for the full CodeRabbit portfolio: Pull Request Reviews, IDE and CLI Reviews, CodeRabbit Security, Change Stack, platform integrations, and agentic change-management workflows.

This is a senior individual-contributor role. You'll set the narrative architecture that makes a growing suite understandable to developers, technical leaders, security teams, and enterprise buyers, and make sure the story holds up in the product, the field, and in customer conversations.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead integrated launches from insight through adoption: message architecture, audience strategy, sales readiness, campaigns, customer education, and post-launch learning.

 - Own portfolio positioning, messaging, personas, and go-to-market strategy. Define how each product earns its place in a single CodeRabbit story.

 - Translate product behavior into clear customer value across reviews, code context, tickets, policies, security findings, and agent-driven change workflows.

 - Lead integrated launches from insight through adoption: message architecture, audience strategy, sales readiness, campaigns, customer education, and post-launch learning.

 - Build the field system behind the story: pitches, demos, evaluation guides, competitive guidance, objection handling, executive materials, and proof for technical buyers.

 - Partner with customers and internal teams to develop credible case studies, benchmarks, usage stories, and evidence that can travel across products and buying stages.

 - Turn competitive analysis into product and GTM decisions, especially around review quality, security, governance, developer trust, and AI-code adoption.

 - Bring structured market and field feedback to Product. Identify recurring friction, missing capabilities, and places where product experience and product story diverge.

 - Raise the standard for technical marketing through hands-on writing, editing, and cross-functional leadership. Mentor other marketers without needing direct-report authority.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing, ideally in developer tools, security, infrastructure, AI, or another technical market.

 - A record of leading complex, multi-product launches and changing how customers understand a category or product suite.

 - Technical fluency and credibility with engineers, product leaders, security teams, and developer audiences.

 - Experience supporting both product-led growth and enterprise sales, including trials, evaluations, customer proof, and executive buying conversations.

 - Excellent writing and editorial judgment, with an instinct for claims that need evidence.

 - A rigorous approach to qualitative customer insight and quantitative product or commercial signals.

 - The ability to turn ambiguity into decisions and bring cross-functional partners with you.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

CodeRabbit has a durable, evidence-backed portfolio narrative that customers and teams can use without translating it for themselves. Each launch reinforces the wider product story. Sales and Customer Success can choose the right proof for reviews, governance, security, local development, and agent workflows. Product gets sharper market feedback, and CodeRabbit's message matches the work engineering teams are actually trying to move forward.


Target salary for the role is $200k-$290k. Actual salary will be based on skills, experience, and location.

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. ABOUT VICE PRESIDENT, PRODUCT MARKETING

CodeRabbit helps engineering teams review, understand, govern, and ship code generated by people and agents.

As AI accelerates code creation, the bottleneck is no longer writing code. The new bottleneck is verifying intent, managing risk, and keeping delivery moving.

We're hiring a VP of Product Marketing to define how the market understands CodeRabbit: the context-aware trust layer between AI-generated code and production. You will turn rapid product innovation into clear customer value, durable differentiation, and measurable go-to-market impact.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own positioning, messaging, segmentation, personas, use cases, and differentiation across CodeRabbit's review, governance, security, planning, and agentic developer workflows.

 - Lead the category shift from human-centric code review to comprehensive code governance and Agentic Change Management.

 - Build and lead launches end to end—from customer insight and product framing through packaging, enablement, content, PR, community, adoption, and field follow-through.

 - Translate technical capabilities and evidence into compelling value stories for developers, engineering leaders, security teams, and executive buyers.

 - Equip Sales and Customer Success with demos, talk tracks, competitive guides, PoV materials, executive narratives, ROI frameworks, and objection handling.

 - Establish a rigorous customer-proof engine spanning case studies, evaluations, benchmarks, analyst relations, and credible proof points.

 - Lead competitive intelligence across AI code review, coding agents, security tools, and the broader software-delivery stack.

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, Growth, Brand, and Finance on roadmap feedback, packaging, monetization, and tier/usage-value communication.

 - Build a high-velocity PMM operating model for major launches, model releases, and category moments.

 - Hire and develop a high-performing PMM team with technical fluency and strong editorial judgment.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 10+ years of B2B SaaS product marketing experience, including senior leadership roles.

 - Deep experience in developer tools, AI, security, DevOps, infrastructure, or technical enterprise software.

 - A record of positioning complex products in crowded markets and moving organizations beyond feature-led messaging.

 - Proven launch and enablement leadership that drove measurable adoption, pipeline, retention, expansion, or revenue.

 - Credibility with engineering, security, product, sales, and executive audiences.

 - Experience supporting both product-led growth and enterprise go-to-market motions.

 - Exceptional writing, storytelling, and analytical judgment grounded in customer research, product data, and competitive evidence.

 - A builder's mindset: strategic at the company level, hands-on when needed, and adaptable when evidence changes.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

CodeRabbit has an evidence-backed category story that makes Agentic Change Management clear, credible, and defensible. Messaging is consistent across product, web, campaigns, sales, and customer success. Launches have clear owners, field readiness, and adoption plans. Sales and Customer Success can carry compelling value stories into PoVs and executive conversations. The market increasingly associates CodeRabbit with high-signal, trustworthy governance of agent-generated code.



Target salary for this role is $250k-$320k. Actual salary will be based on candidate skills, experience and location.
